advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether module-size analyzer specs should short-circuit to unavailable when `code_health.enabled` is False, and gate the scc invocation on it if so.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:164 `def compute(ctx: Any) -> Any:` then `result = scc_loc.analyze(Path(ctx.repo_root), ctx.scan_roots)` with no check of an enabled flag
src/rebar/_config_schema.py:557 `enabled: bool = False` — CodeHealthConfig defaults to disabled

ABSENCE: `search_files` for `enabled` under src/rebar/metrics returned no matches, and metrics.py builds ctx from scan_roots/size_cap/size_near_fraction only (src/rebar/_commands/metrics.py:140-147), omitting `code_health.enabled`.
advisory.finding: The new module-size metrics run the scc analyzer unconditionally and never consult `code_health.enabled`, so scc is executed even when code-health is configured as disabled (the default `enabled=False`).
scenarios: A repo that has not opted into code-health (enabled=False) still triggers scc subprocess invocations on every `rebar metrics` run.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the intended default scan scope; empty scan_roots now scans the whole repo root instead of the source tree.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/scc_loc.py:63-65 `candidates = [] if scan_roots is None else list(scan_roots)` then `if not candidates: candidates = [repo_root]`
src/rebar/_config_schema.py:558 `scan_roots: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)` — default is empty, which triggers the whole-repo fallback
advisory.finding: When `scan_roots` is empty (the default), the analyzer falls back to scanning the entire repository root, a behavior change from the previous metric which scanned only `src/rebar/**/*.py`.
scenarios: Default config (empty scan_roots) counts every scc-recognized file across the whole repo — including tests, vendored, and non-Python languages — into count/max_loc/over_cap_count.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting `churn` and `refactor_to_addition_ratio` are registered in REGISTRY with source='git' and lens='code_health' (restore the coverage lost when `test_git_metrics_registered_with_labels` was deleted).
evidence: Deleted test asserted registration+provenance for git metrics: named = {"module_size_distribution", "churn", "cap_change_events", "refactor_to_addition_ratio"} ... assert git_specs[mid].source == "git"

Replacement only covers new analyzer specs: `for metric_id in ("module_size_distribution", "oversized_module_count"): ... assert matches[0].source == "structural"` (tests/unit/metrics/test_git_metrics_heldout.py:130-137)

git_metrics.py:189-190 register() still appends `_git_spec("churn", churn)` and `_git_spec("refactor_to_addition_ratio", refactor_to_addition_ratio)` — the diff changed this registration path but no test now pins that these ids land in REGISTRY with source='git'

tests/interfaces/test_metrics_cli.py:44-49 iterates `registered = {spec.id for spec in REGISTRY}` and asserts only `set(metrics.keys()) >= registered` — vacuously true if churn is absent from REGISTRY
advisory.finding: The refactor of the git-sourced spec adapter (`_spec(...ranged=True)` -> `_git_spec(...)`) and the deletion of `test_git_metrics_registered_with_labels` leave NO test asserting that `churn` and `refactor_to_addition_ratio` are registered into REGISTRY with source='git'/lens='code_health'. The replacement `test_provenance_and_no_dup_seed` pins provenance only for the two new analyzer specs; `test_metrics_json_covers_every_registered_id` iterates whatever set is registered and cannot detect a git metric being dropped from `register()`.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_git_metrics_heldout.py add: `git_specs = {s.id: s for s in REGISTRY if s.source == 'git'}; for mid in ('churn','refactor_to_addition_ratio'): assert mid in git_specs and git_specs[mid].lens == 'code_health' and git_specs[mid].source == 'git'`.
